answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a refundable stake that is slashed if peers catch it forge duplicate identities. A newcomer starts with only a whisper of trust, tiny limits that grow solely through verified useful work over time. A zephyr of cheap fake accounts cannot accumulate the history or the stake honest agents build, so each extra identity costs real money while earning almost nothing, turning identity creation from free into a priced decision.
